## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* is the sixteenth and concluding section of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 16) in the Khuddaka Nikāya, providing a detailed canonical commentary on the *Sāriputta Sutta*. In modern grammatical and chronological studies of canonical Pali literature, the text is cited for its distinctive verbal morphology, including aorist forms derived from the root *budh* such as *bujjhi*, *anubujjhi*, *paṭibujjhi*, *sambujjhi*, and *sammābujjhi* [Kingsbury 2002].

 In addition, shared passages connect with suttas such as the *Sabbāsava Sutta* (MN 2) and *Āsavasutta* (AN 6.58), the *Nettippakaraṇa*, and various recensions of the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* tradition across Pali, Sanskrit, Gāndhārī, and Chinese.
